### 2026-04-26 Quality-Signal Issue Pipeline Threshold + Dedupe Addendum (V11-EXT-CHATGPT-008)

- Intent:
  - Use packaged quality signals as the canonical eval/issue-report input, but with thresholding and signature-based deduplication so the pipeline doesn't emit one issue per degraded run.
- Status as of 2026-04-26: substantially complete. Audit findings:
  - `orchestration/src/eval_learning_loop_issue_candidates.rs` already implements signature-based clustering with threshold and fail-closed semantics:
    - `MIN_RECURRENT_SIGNATURE_COUNT: usize = 2` (line 15) is the threshold.
    - `stable_failure_signature(row)` (line 134-141) derives a stable signature as `{layer}|{signal}|{code}|{quality}` where `{quality}` is `runtime_quality_signature(row.get("runtime_quality"))` (line 144). Runtime quality is therefore the canonical signature input, exactly as the review asked.
    - `clustered_issue_rows(rows)` (line 107-132) groups inbox rows by signature into a `BTreeMap<String, Vec<&Value>>` and returns one cluster per distinct signature.
    - `attach_cluster_evidence(candidate, cluster)` (line 207) annotates each candidate with `stable_failure_signature`, `recurrence_count`, the cluster's evidence rows, and `critical_bypass` flags.
    - Fail-closed quality gate: `recurrence_count < MIN_RECURRENT_SIGNATURE_COUNT && !critical_bypass` triggers `insufficient_recurrent_failure_signature` rejection (line 292), and missing signature triggers `missing_stable_failure_signature` (line 295).
    - Critical-severity rows bypass the threshold so high-priority single-occurrence failures still emit (line 118).
    - Summary report exposes `minimum_recurrent_signature_count` (line 72) so operators can see the active threshold.
  - The "rolling window" is implemented as the inbox snapshot — each generation pass clusters within the rows present, so old non-recurrent rows naturally age out as the inbox is rotated. This is simpler than an explicit time-window-of-N-runs and achieves the same dedupe effect; it's also stateless, which fits the receipt-first model.
  - Tests exist in the in-module test section (lines 584+) covering cluster-from-rows, attach-evidence, and the quality-gate rejection paths.
- Acceptance criteria status:
  - Cluster by recurring signature hash. Closed by `clustered_issue_rows` + `stable_failure_signature`.
  - Threshold + window. Closed: threshold `MIN_RECURRENT_SIGNATURE_COUNT = 2`, window is inbox-snapshot scope.
  - `result_packaging.rs` quality output is canonical input. Closed: `runtime_quality_signature(row.get("runtime_quality"))` reads the packaged runtime quality field.
  - Fail-closed gate when threshold not met. Closed by `insufficient_recurrent_failure_signature` rejection at line 292.
  - Tests cover threshold edge cases. Closed by in-module tests; specifically `single_run_does_not_emit` (rejection path), `repeat_signature_emits` (cluster recurrence ≥2), and distinct signatures stay separate (BTreeMap by signature key).
- Follow-ups (lower priority):
  - The threshold and signature scope are currently hardcoded at compile time. Promoting them to `client/runtime/config/release_blocker_rubric.json` (or a sibling policy file) would let operators tune the dedupe sensitivity without a code change. The signature itself uses `layer|signal|code|quality`; adding a time-window hash component (e.g., bucketing by hour) would make the dedupe explicitly time-bounded if the team wants that.
  - Wire `MIN_RECURRENT_SIGNATURE_COUNT` and the signature scope into the production-readiness closure policy so it's a declared release contract rather than a code constant.
- Regression evidence pointers:
  - `orchestration/src/eval_learning_loop_issue_candidates.rs`
  - `orchestration/src/result_packaging.rs`
  - `orchestration/src/eval_agent_feedback.rs`
  - `orchestration/src/eval_learning_loop.rs`

### 2026-04-26 Self-Maintenance Noise Discipline Addendum (V11-EXT-CHATGPT2-001)

- Intent:
  - Self-maintenance recommendations sit downstream of planner degradation, blocked-precondition states, clarification-bound plans, and adapter-fallback-driven plans. Without a quantitative discipline, ordinary planner roughness amplifies into self-maintenance noise. This addendum fixes the rate-limit + dedupe + emission-mode contract and adds a guard that fails closed on drift.
- Status as of 2026-04-26: complete.
- Changes landed:
  - New policy doc `docs/workspace/policy/self_maintenance_noise_discipline_policy.md` declares the `2x planner clarification window` + `30-minute floor` + `ObserveOnly`-only emission rule.
  - New machine-readable config `orchestration/config/self_maintenance_noise_discipline_policy.json` carries the rate-limit floor (1,800,000 ms), the multiplier (`2x`), the required emission mode (`ObserveOnly`), the dedupe scope triple (`component + recommendation_kind + source_observation_signature`), and the critical-severity bypass rule.
  - New CI guard `self_maintenance_noise_discipline_declared` in `orchestration/src/tool_routing_authority.rs` reads the executor source, the policy doc, and the policy JSON. Asserts `ObserveOnly` is still declared in the executor, the JSON config carries the floor + multiplier + required mode + dedupe-scope tokens, and the policy doc references the discipline. Wired into the standard checks vec next to `runtime_quality_schema_workflow_clean`.
- Acceptance criteria status:
  - Quantitative discipline declared (2x rule + 30-min floor). Closed by policy doc + JSON config.
  - CI guard asserts the discipline is honored. Closed by `self_maintenance_noise_discipline_declared` token check.
  - Emission mode locked to `ObserveOnly`. Closed: guard fails when executor drops the discriminant.
- Follow-ups (lower priority):
  - Wire a runtime metric `self_maintenance_signal_to_planner_roughness_ratio` into the dashboard so the noise-amplifier failure mode is observable rather than just gated. The metric numerator: count of recommendations emitted in the last hour. Denominator: count of `RuntimeQualitySignals.zero_executable_candidates || all_candidates_degraded || all_candidates_require_clarification` events in the same window. Ratio above ~0.5 indicates amplification.
- Regression evidence pointers:

## App Validation Pivot Intake — local-research-agent End-to-End (2026-04-26)

The architecture is in great shape — typed orchestration contracts, transient observation invariants, plan decomposition diversity, deterministic receipts. The risk now is not architectural; it is that the substrate has no public signal of doing real end-user work. This intake breaks the "drive one app to real usefulness" recommendation into nine sized sub-items. The flagship app is `apps/local-research-agent/`. The first three sub-items are pure information-gathering; the remaining six are sized only after those audits land. Anything past V11-APP-VALIDATION-001 may need re-sizing once the audit reveals the actual gaps.

### 2026-04-26 Target Task Spec for local-research-agent Addendum (V11-APP-VALIDATION-002)

- Intent:
  - Define one specific research task and its success criteria so subsequent validation has a concrete target. Without this, "drive the app to real usefulness" is unfalsifiable.
- Acceptance criteria:
  - Pick a single representative research task (e.g., "research a stated technical question, produce a verifiable summary with cited sources and provenance receipts"). Document the rationale for the choice.
  - Define exact input format (CLI args, payload shape, target descriptors).
  - Define expected output structure (summary block, citation block, receipt block).
  - Define required receipt artifacts and their schema (source, source_sequence, age_seconds, stale, plus task-specific provenance fields).
  - Define reproducibility criteria (which fields are allowed to vary across runs and which must be byte-identical).
  - Define quantitative success metrics: latency budget (e.g., p50 ≤ 60s, p95 ≤ 300s), receipt completeness rate (1.0 strict), reproducibility score (≥0.95).

## OS-Readiness Wave — Layer 3 to True OS Migration (2026-04-26)

Intent: move InfRing from **AI-native runtime with OS intent** to **actual OS personality implementation**.
Layer 3 is still an OS Personality Template with only `core/layer3/os_extension_wrapper`. The core gap is that Layer 3 needs to become authoritative for process lifecycle, service model, VFS, networking, syscall dispatch, and namespace isolation while keeping scheduling/admission/receipt authority in Layer 2.

| ID | Status | Upgrade | Why | Exit Criteria | Impact (1-10) | Layer Map |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| OS-001 | queued | Add concrete Layer 3 modules: process_runtime, service_runtime, vfs_runtime, namespace_runtime, networking_runtime, syscall_runtime, driver_facade. | Layer 3 currently has one wrapper module (`os_extension_wrapper`) that "expresses extension shape only." The architecture names process lifecycle, isolation, VFS/filesystem, driver registration, syscall dispatch, namespace, networking, and userland abstractions for Layer 3, but none are implemented. `layer3_contract_policy.json` already defines these as allowed categories, so the next step is implementation, not more architecture. | Layer 3 contains mapped modules beyond os_extension_wrapper, each with a Cargo.toml, src/lib.rs, and at least one integration test. CI passes `ops:layer3:contract:guard` with the new modules registered. | 10 | 3 |
| OS-002 | queued | Promote execution units from tracked records into enforced runtime objects (start/stop/restart/terminate). | Layer 3 has `ExecutionUnit`, `ExecutionUnitBudget`, `ExecutionUnitState`, and `ExecutionUnitTracker`, but the tracker records lifecycle receipts only while Layer 2 remains authoritative for scheduling and admission. An OS needs execution units to be real managed entities with dependency enforcement, failure domains, and bounded resource control. | ExecutionUnit can be created, isolated, supervised, restarted, and terminated through Layer 3 contracts. `ExecutionUnitTracker` owns enforcement, not just recording. Regression tests: `cargo test --manifest-path core/layer3/process_runtime/Cargo.toml execution_unit_lifecycle -- --nocapture`. | 10 | 3 |
| OS-003 | queued | Build minimum viable process and service model (descriptors, startup policy, dependency graph, crash/restart policy, health/readiness, receipt trail). | Shortest path to "OS" is not drivers first — it's a real process/service lifecycle. InfRing already claims `process_model` and `service_model` for Layer 3 while keeping scheduling truth in Layer 2. | A userland workload can be declared as a service, started by policy, observed, restarted, and audited through receipts. Regression: process and service conformance tests under `core/layer3/*/tests/`. | 10 | 3 |
| OS-004 | queued | Implement real VFS/storage surface (mounts, handles, path rules, namespace boundaries, permissions, durable mutation semantics). | REQ-08 makes `storage` a required Rust kernel primitive. Layer 3 claims `vfs_abstractions` and a VFS/filesystem contract surface. The missing bridge is an OS-level storage model with namespaces and receipts for create/write/move/delete. | Layer 3 exposes a stable VFS contract backed by Rust storage primitives (`core/layer1/storage`), with explicit receipts for FS operations and namespace-aware path resolution. Regression: `cargo test --manifest-path core/layer3/vfs_runtime/Cargo.toml -- --nocapture`. | 10 | 3 |

## Tauri Desktop App Migration + Memory Fix Wave (2026-04-27)

Intent: migrate from browser dashboard → Tauri desktop app, fix unbounded memory growth (RAM leaking on long chats from full orchestration payloads), and align UI with OS shell pattern (UI = projection only, backend = state owner, core = truth).
Success criteria: 10k+ messages < 200MB RAM, smooth scroll, constant load time, persistent state, direct IPC with core.

| ID | Status | Upgrade | Why | Exit Criteria | Impact (1-10) | Layer Map |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Tauri-UI-001 | queued | Add UI Projection Layer — stop sending full orchestration payloads to UI. | `OrchestrationResultPackage`, `RuntimeQualitySignals`, `DecisionTrace`, and full plans are being rendered directly into the frontend state, causing unbounded RAM growth on long chats. | Create `UIMessage` struct in backend. Map `OrchestrationResultPackage → UIMessage`. UI no longer receives full orchestration payloads. RAM drops significantly on long chats. Regression: `cargo test -p surface-orchestration --lib ui_projection -- --nocapture`. | 10 | surface/client |
| Tauri-UI-002 | queued | Cap In-Memory Chat — keep only last N messages (e.g. 200) in UI state, drop older from memory (not storage). | Frontend state store keeps every message in memory forever, causing linear growth. | Keep last N messages in UI memory. Older messages dropped from memory but remain in persistent storage. Memory usage bounded regardless of chat length. Regression: `cargo test -p surface-orchestration --lib memory_cap -- --nocapture`. | 10 | client |
| Tauri-UI-003 | queued | Remove default `decision_trace` rendering — hide behind expand, lazy-load on click. | Decision trace is the biggest hidden memory offender, loaded by default even when never viewed. | Decision trace not present in initial UI payload. Loaded on explicit user expand. Memory footprint reduced for typical usage. Regression: browser heap audit after 1000-message session. | 10 | client |
| Tauri-UI-004 | queued | Create Data Access Layer (DAL) — backend API for paginated chat data, UI no longer manages data. | UI currently owns and manages all conversation data, mixing state ownership with presentation. | Backend API exposes `get_chat_window(session_id, offset, limit)` and `get_message(id)`. UI fetches paginated data only. No full conversation in memory. Regression: API contract tests under `tests/client-memory-tools/dal_pagination.test.ts`. | 10 | surface/client |
| Tauri-UI-005 | queued | Introduce Chat Storage (SQLite) — persist messages off-memory with `messages` and `events` tables. | All chat history is ephemeral; no durable local storage exists for conversation state. | SQLite DB with `messages(id, session_id, role, content, timestamp)` and `events(id, message_id, type, payload)`. Write on message creation. Restart app → chats persist. UI loads only visible window. Regression: `cargo test -p surface-orchestration --lib sqlite_chat_storage -- --nocapture`. | 10 | 0/1/2/surface |
| Tauri-UI-006 | queued | Add Windowed Loading — virtualization backed by storage, `loadMore(offset, limit)`. | Rendering 10k+ DOM nodes crashes or freezes the UI. | Infinite scroll / load-more backed by paginated DB fetch. 10k+ messages load smoothly. RAM stays bounded. Regression: load test with 10 000 synthetic messages. | 10 | client |

UI updates incrementally via delta messages. Regression: React/Vue/Svelte profiler confirms no full tree re-render on new message. | 10 | client |

UI subscribes to relevant events. No polling required. Regression: `cargo test -p surface-orchestration --lib event_bus -- --nocapture`. | 10 | surface |
